title: Operatorless onboarding + sparse-audit flow (PRD draft)
body:
Purpose
------
This is a working PRD for an operatorless onboarding flow for customer-managed VPCs that minimizes audit log volume (sparse-audit) while preserving forensic value for compliance teams. Target: SMB & mid-market customers who want self-service Private deployment onboarding without a manual operator review for low-risk changes, but with robust gates for higher-risk events.

Problem statement
-----------------
Today onboarding and small network changes require an operator to verify artifacts and attach audit evidence. This is a blocker for self-serve customers and increases lead time. At the same time, retaining full verbose telemetry across all onboarding events is costly and exposes more customer data than necessary. Need: a model that reduces manual work + storage costs while keeping enough evidence to investigate incidents and satisfy audits.

Goals (measurable)
------------------
- Reduce operator intervention for initial onboarding to <15% of installs within 6 months of launch.
- Cut onboarding-related audit logs retained in Redwood storage by ~60% for eligible customers.
- Maintain mean time to investigate (MTTI) for onboarding incidents within SLA (48h) using compact evidence bundles.
- Provide cryptographic receipts customers can store on their side for non-repudiation.

User stories
-----------
- As a platform engineer at CustomerCo, I want a self-serve onboarding wizard that validates my VPC handoff and returns a signed receipt so I don't wait for Redwood ops.
- As an internal compliance reviewer, I want a way to request the full evidence pack within 90 days so I can audit a change if warranted.
- As an SRE, I want confidence that the sparse-audit extractor captures artifacts necessary to reconstruct session-level decisions if we need to debug.

Scope / non-goals
-----------------
In scope: onboarding handshake, lightweight approval heuristics, sparse-audit serializer, customer receipt format, escalation path to full operator review.
Out of scope: full SIEM integrations (later), long-term cold archive policies (separate MLP).

High-level design
-----------------
1) Risk classifier at handoff: client-provided metadata + pass/fail checks (CIDR overlap, unexpected ports, pre-approved ASN) -> risk score {low, medium, high}.
2) For low-risk: issue operatorless onboarding with compact evidence bundle (CEB) and signed receipt. Store CEB for 30 days, redact PII, index minimal search keys.
3) For medium/high: create automatic approval ticket to operations and instruct customer to provide supplemental artifacts; keep verbose telemetry until resolution.
4) Evidence pack formats: CEB (JSON LZ4 gz, signed with customer and Redwood keys, contains hashes of configs + compressed conntrace snippets) and Full Evidence (raw telemetry + packet metadata) available on request with audit justification.

Requirements (must have)
-----------------------
- UX: onboarding flow exposes risk rationale and checkbox to opt into operatorless onboarding.
- Crypto: receipts signed with Redwood KMS key + customer public key if provided.
- Retention: CEB kept by Redwood for at least 30 days; archived full evidence kept per contract if requested.
- Controls: customer can opt-out of operatorless flow and force manual review.
- Observability: dashboards for rates of operatorless success, false positives, and escalation latency.

Telemetry & logs (sparse patterns)
--------------------------------
- Store only event-level hashes and pointers for low-risk flows: metadata fields (timestamp, vpc-id hash, operatorless-flag, risk-score).
- Capture sample of raw traces (1 in N) for low-risk on randomized rolling windows to preserve diagnostic capability.
- All retained CEBs are flagged immutable and include compact provenance (who initiated, which UI step, accepted terms).

Approval gate heuristics (sketch)
--------------------------------
- Hard gates: CIDR overlap with Redwood-managed ranges, use of reserved ports, requesting private peering -> auto escalate.
- Soft gates: new ASN, unusual region, or security policy exceptions -> allow operatorless if customer has pre-approval policy configured (org-level allowlist).

Rollout plan
------------
- Phase 0 (experiment): select 5 pilot accounts; manual opt-in; ops shadow mode. 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: beta (50 customers) with partial automation + visible dashboards; monitor false positives. 6 weeks.
- Phase 2: GA with org-level allowlists and UI affordances; enable default operatorless for eligible customers. 8–12 weeks after beta.

Success metrics
---------------
- Operatorless adoption rate, operator interventions avoided, CEB storage size reduction, incident MTTI.

Security & compliance notes
--------------------------
- CEB redaction rules must be minimally sufficient for forensics; legal consulted on what constitutes PII.
- Provide customers export option for receipts and CEB for their own archival.

Risks & mitigations
-------------------
- Risk: missed malicious configuration due to sampling. Mitigate: conservative risk thresholds + immediate escalation if signals cross.
- Risk: regulatory objection to short retention. Mitigate: contract SLA options for extended retention; preserve hashed indexes for longer.

Open questions (to decide)
-------------------------
- Default retention window for CEB across regions (30 vs 90 days).
- Acceptance criteria for org-level allowlist vs per-change approvals.
- How to integrate with existing attestation/ledger work without duplicating effort.

Next steps / owners
-------------------
- Product: finalize heuristics and UX copy (Priya) by 2025-03-07.
- Eng: prototype CEB serializer and signing flow (Liam) by 2025-03-21.
- SRE: sampling policy and dashboard metrics (Sofia) by 2025-03-14.
- Legal: redaction checklist and retention guidance (Ethan) by 2025-03-10.

Notes to self
------------
- Shadow-mode logs live under s3://redwood-priv/onboard-shadow/ for now.
- Reference: JIRA-PRIV-201 (attestation ledger spike), confluence: /privnet-onboard-archive.
- Keep this doc short; move detailed schema into a separate "CEB-schema.md".

End of draft.
